sentences.text: In this backdrop he urges the Court to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
6. Per contra, learned APP for the State has argued on the lines of the status report.
7. I have heard the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner as well as learned APP for the State and have perused the record.
8. A perusal of the testimony of PW1 shows that on 19.05.2022 when he visited the matrimonial home of the deceased, only the parents of the petitioner and his brother were present.

Prima facie it appears that no specific allegations have been made by PW1 against the petitioner as regard the demand made on 19.05.2022 during his visit or apropos the incident of suicide which was also committed by the deceased on the same day.

9. It is in the testimony of PW1 and PW2 that brother and parents of the petitioner were at home when the incident happened, which gives an This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/11/2023 at 10:23:03 inference that the petitioner was not at home when the deceased committed suicide.
10. Further, the prosecution has cited as many as 26 witnesses, of which only 02 witnesses have been examined.
The petitioner is also facing incarceration since 23.05.2022.
Needless to say that the trial of the case is going to be a protracted one.

Delay in commencement and conclusion of trial is a factor to be taken into account at the stage of considering bail application and the accused cannot be kept in custody for indefinite period if trial is not likely to be concluded within reasonable time.
11. It is trite law that apart from other factors, peculiar facts of each case can be taken into account while deciding the application for bail.
This Court cannot be unmindful of the fact that the petitioner has two minor children aged about 1  years and 03 years and the mother of the children has committed suicide.
The petitioner being in custody, there is no parent available to take care of them and to cater to their needs.
12. It is not the case of the prosecution that the petitioner is a flight risk.
Further, the parents of the deceased having been examined, there is no apprehension that the petitioner will influence the trial if released on bail.
13. Having regard to the circumstances discussed above, the petitioner has made out a case for grant of regular bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner is admitted to bail subject to his furnishing a Personal Bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- and one Surety Bond of the like amount subject to the satisfaction of the Trial Court / Jail Superintendent/Duty Magistrate, further subject to the following conditions:-
a) Petitioner/applicant will not leave the city without prior permission of the Court.
